rationale: wu_2015_trainable-claude-agentic: wu_n_bands=6, wu_n_outer=1, lr=0.01, epochs=6, batch_size=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214, grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, seed=42, rationale=wu_2015_trainable iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). SIX-BOX (NUMBERS). (1) PRIOR: iter-1 = SSIM 0.8370 / hr 0.0508, 8 params (wu_n_bands=4, wu_n_outer=1, ep6, lr0.01), elapsed 335s. iter-2 = SSIM 0.8390 / hr 0.0337, 8 params (SAME but ep18), elapsed 866.6s. iter-1->iter-2 (epochs 6->18) was FLAT: val_ssim +0.0020 (within the +-0.001 noise band the iter-2 falsifier set), and hr actually FELL 0.0508->0.0337. Per-epoch train cost = (866.6-335)/(18-6) = 44.3 s/ep at n_bands=4. SLURM log confirms training converged (loss=0.00000 by ep1; band_scale already saturating to clamp by ep18) -- epochs is INERT, the falsifier for under-training FIRED. (2) FAILURE MODE: few-param tuned-FBP ceiling. Wu-trainable is a band-reweighted aliasing-free FBP + ONE soft-thresholded dense residual pass with NO image-domain CNN denoiser; it sits hr~0.04 just above the LD-FBP floor and epochs cannot move it. The OPEN question iter-2's falsifier handed to iter-3: is hr capacity-limited (too few frequency bands to separate signal from noise) or is the whole FBP-family structurally ceilinged regardless of capacity? (3) ONE KNOB: CAPACITY via wu_n_bands 4->6 (+2 frequency bands in the band-weighted aliasing-free FBP, line 198 band-loop). This is the iter-2 falsifier's prescribed lever ('iter-3 must add capacity, wu_n_bands up'). I deliberately pick wu_n_bands over wu_n_outer because (a) n_bands enriches the FBP frequency partition -- the exact structurally-FBP part the ceiling hypothesis is about; (b) it is BUDGET-SAFE: the band-loop (FFT-filter + back_project) scales LINEARLY with n_bands while the heavy dense-projector residual pass stays a single fixed pass at n_outer=1, vs wu_n_outer++ which DOUBLES that dominant cost; (c) wu_n_outer=1 is the campaign 'mandatory' hint, leave it. NEW PARAM COUNT: wu_n_bands+2+2*wu_n_outer = 6+2+2*1 = 10 trainable scalars (was 8). epochs held at the iter-1 anchor 6 (NOT a second knob -- iter-2 PROVED ep6 vs ep18 is a non-difference, 0.837 vs 0.839; reverting to ep6 restores the proven-equivalent baseline epoch budget so the wider 6-band bank fits the HARD 20-min wall with margin, isolating n_bands as the sole meaningful change). All else identical to iter-1/2: lr0.01, bs=1, val_chunk=1, train_n=200, val_n=214(ALL L277), grad_clip=1.0, lambda_neg=1.0, weight_decay=0.0, loss_base=mse, seed=42. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if iter-3 SSIM rises measurably above 0.839 (>+0.005 over the noise band) with hr>0.05, Wu-trainable was frequency-band-capacity-limited and more bands buy real headroom. FALSIFIER: if SSIM REGRESSES or stays FLAT (<=0.840, within noise of iter-1/2) at 6 bands, Wu-trainable is STRUCTURALLY FBP-ceilinged on Mayo regardless of capacity -- exactly matching the few-param-bilateral pattern THIS tick (dual_domain_bilateral_supervised img_n_bf 3->6: 0.9192->0.9057 REGRESSED; hammernik filters-up also regressed), i.e. capacity bumps DESTABILISE these few-param FBP-family denoisers rather than help. A regression would be the strong confirmation that the lever is the FBP family itself, not its band count. (5) HARD 20-min (1200s) train+score budget, sized via the ep6 anchor: worst-case (whole per-sample cost scaling with n_bands, which over-counts since the residual pass is fixed) ~1.5x the iter-1 per-epoch -> ~66 s/ep x 6 = ~396s train + ~120s for the 1.5x-wider 214-slice val pass ~= 520s, with the val FIGURE outside the budget and well under the 1800s SLURM kill. val = ALL 214 L277 slices (do NOT reduce); grad_clip=1.0; bs=1 + val_chunk=1 forced by per-sample-ps; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted; per-sample-ps FBP + per-sample model.proj/model.dense_proj swap; bg_target=truth; 321px detector-geometry FOV default (NO fov override). (6) no control return.
